summary.oneLiner: Orient Bell leveraged the Morbi gas crisis to drive a 20% price hike and expand EBITDA margins by 270 bps YoY, shifting from a rate-driven to a sell-out model. With a debt-free balance sheet and 60-65% utilization, the company is positioned to capture market share from distressed unorganized players while sustaining margin expansion through operating leverage.
summary.business: Orient Bell Limited manufactures and sells ceramic wall and floor tiles and vitrified tiles, including glazed vitrified tiles (GVT), through strategically located manufacturing facilities and an extensive retail network across India. The Company sells to home-owners, dealers and channel partners as well as institutional/project customers, with sales routed through its Orient Bell Tile Boutique (OBTB/OBTX) retail network and a wider dealer channel. Internally the business is run as ceramic and vitrified-polished divisions, and it has extended into tile adhesives and bonding chemicals under the 'Master Bond' brand; the Company reports a total manufacturing capacity of 42.4 MSM per annum, over 4,000 SKUs and more than 2,000 business partners.

Vitrified tiles: GVT Aurum (600x1200 mm tile made using a dry process)

The only stated capital-return intent is an ordinary-business resolution at the 49th Annual General Meeting to declare a dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended 31st March 2026. On executive pay, the proposed re-appointment of the Chairman and Whole Time Director carries a graded salary scale with an annual increment plus a commission on net profits to be determined by the Nomination & Remuneration Committee / Board, and the Company operates an ESOP Scheme 2021 under which options were granted during the year at an exercise price of Rs. 10 per option.|Workplace safety is run to a stated 'zero harm' objective, with adherence to safety protocols as the mitigation for workplace safety risk|Investment in sustainable and energy-efficient practices is the stated mitigation for environmental and sustainability expectations|Energy management is an explicit lever in the operational excellence programme, contributing to the 3.2% like-for-like reduction in production costs in FY26|Structured learning and development for employees to build capability and prepare future leadership, guided by the 'Sarv Neta Vikreta' philosophy, alongside a commitment to a safe, inclusive, transparent and performance-oriented workplace across a workforce of 781 employees as of March 31, 2026
currentContext.expansion: The annual report discloses no new greenfield plant, brownfield line or capacity-addition project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Installed footprint is described only as a total manufacturing capacity of 42.4 MSM per annum. Expansion in FY26 is channel-, product- and platform-led rather than capacity-led: the Company strengthened its retail-led growth strategy through Orient Bell Tile Boutiques, where the focus during FY26 was on improving the quality, size and productivity of existing showrooms along with selective expansion in key markets, and deepened its presence in the Western region while maintaining its core North and East India markets; it is actively expanding the dealer network across South India, supported by brand-building and marketing. On the product side, the Company piloted tile adhesives during the year and, after the pilot launch, adhesives are being rolled out across markets and are expected to scale up gradually - an entry into adhesives and bonding chemicals under the 'Master Bond' brand explicitly framed as building on the established distribution system while keeping capital investment low. Portfolio expansion took the form of 526 new GVT SKUs and 247 ceramic SKUs launched in FY26 rather than new lines. The Company also continued to invest in digital and AI platforms for content, channel partners and the sales force, and in national brand building. Financially, disciplined capital allocation and healthy cash generation kept the Company net debt-free, described as providing adequate financial flexibility to support future growth opportunities.

risks.risk: Industry overcapacity and price-based competition, especially from the Morbi cluster
risks.note: Morbi continues to face overcapacity with periodic shutdowns indicating imbalanced supply-demand, which leads to price-cutting and 'dumping' of stock in the domestic market and pressures average selling prices. Management lists intense competition, price pressure from excess supply and dealer inventory risk among its industry and market risks, mitigated through premiumisation, stronger dealer relationships, agile pricing and demand-led production planning.

risks.risk: Dependence on natural gas / PNG-LNG fuel cost and supply
risks.note: High dependence on fuel costs directly impacts margins, and any disruption in PNG/LNG supply chains can halt production, with limited alternative energy substitution options at scale. FY26 saw heightened volatility in natural gas prices at year-end due to geopolitical tensions and supply disruptions in West Asia; the Company's long-term gas contracts and sourcing arrangements are the stated buffer.

risks.risk: Cyclicality tied to real estate and a subdued demand environment
risks.note: Demand is linked to the real estate cycle; the year began with muted domestic demand, slower real estate activity and pricing pressure from excess industry capacity, and volumes only recovered in the second half as projects progressed towards the finishing stage.

risks.risk: Overdependence on the core tile segment
risks.note: Listed by management as a strategic risk alongside evolving consumer preferences and the need for innovation and differentiation; the mitigation is diversification into adhesives and bonding chemicals under 'Master Bond' plus investment in product innovation and premium, value-added offerings.

risks.risk: Sub-scale versus larger industry players, and weakness in the institutional/project segment
risks.note: Management flags limited scale compared to larger industry players as an operational risk that affects margins, together with challenges in institutional/project segment performance; mitigation is cost optimisation, efficiency improvements and stabilisation of institutional business teams.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration - weak/mixed South India performance
risks.note: While the Company strengthened its position in western markets, South India performance was mixed with growth in certain regions remaining subdued; the dealer network there is being expanded with focused brand-building and marketing.

risks.risk: Brand awareness gap versus established competitors
risks.note: The Company's brand awareness across diverse consumer segments in India is comparatively lower than certain established competitors, addressed through expanded national television advertising and a consistent on-air presence through the year.

The Middle East remains a key export market for Indian tiles and any escalation in regional conflicts can delay or stop construction projects, while further geopolitical fragmentation creates regional supply chain blocks; rising protectionist trade measures including tariffs and USD/INR volatility are described as a structural macroeconomic risk to costs and margins. Global competition, including Chinese players in export markets, is also flagged.

risks.risk: Margin, working capital and liquidity risk from cost volatility
risks.note: Financial risks flagged are pressure on margins due to cost volatility, working capital management challenges and liquidity risk; mitigation is a strong balance sheet with healthy cash and cash equivalents, a 20-day working capital cycle and disciplined capital allocation.

Exposure to economic fluctuations, regulatory changes, geopolitical developments, currency volatility and financial market conditions, plus risks from delays in approvals, litigation and reputational issues; managed through continuous monitoring of the external environment, compliance frameworks, diversified market presence and proactive legal and reputational risk management.

one-line thesis: Orient Bell leveraged the Morbi gas crisis to drive a 20% price hike and expand EBITDA margins by 270 bps YoY, shifting from a rate-driven to a sell-out model. With a debt-free balance sheet and 60-65% utilization, the company is positioned to capture market share from distressed unorganized players while sustaining margin expansion through operating leverage.
financial scorecard: Revenue +7.5% YoY (Q4), +3.1% YoY (FY26); EBITDA +66% YoY to INR 16.4cr (Margin 7.7%, +270bps); PAT (PBT) INR 8.4cr vs INR 3.6cr YoY; Order Book: N/A (Retail/Project mix 78:22); Net Debt: Negative INR 29cr (Cash rich). One-offs: INR 1.3cr charge for new labor code compliance in FY26.
guidance: No formal numerical guidance; Management expects margin trajectory to continue QoQ; Capex limited to maintenance (INR 10cr +/- INR 4-5cr for FY27); Volume growth dependent on gas availability and Morbi normalization.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable for B2C/B2B hybrid model; Retail contributes ~78% of revenue; Institutional/Project segment underperformed in FY26; Dealer inventory cautious due to 20% price hike working capital squeeze.
segment / subsidiary detail: Vitrified capacity utilization ~80%; Ceramic lines ~90%; Adhesives in pilot/expansion phase across North & East India with new epoxy/grout launches; Anti-static tiles gaining traction but negligible revenue contribution currently.
growth verticals / optionality: Market share consolidation from unorganized/Morbi players shutting down; Geographic expansion of Adhesives segment; Digital lead generation converting 350+ dealers monthly; Premium mix shift via AI visualization tools.
margins & cost dynamics: Gas prices averaged INR 45/SCM in Q4 (up ~30% YoY); Power & Fuel cost up 34% YoY driven by 20-25% production volume increase; 20% price hike (March/April) fully offset input cost inflation; Marketing spend at 3.6%, targeting ~4%.
capex / expansion: FY26 actuals INR 6-7cr; FY27 guidance INR 10cr (+/- 4-5cr) strictly for maintenance; No greenfield/brownfield capacity expansion planned due to sufficient idle capacity (operating at 60-65%).
capital allocation: Debt-free status achieved with negative net debt of INR 29cr; Strong cash conversion cycle improved to 20 days (from 26); DSO reduced by 9 days to 48 days; Focus on working capital discipline and liquidity for M&A or organic opportunities.
risks & watch-items: Sustained high gas prices impacting demand elasticity; Labor shortages in Morbi delaying competitor recovery; Short-term demand blips due to interest rate hikes/austerity; Dealer inventory de-stocking due to price volatility.
management quality / tone: Cautiously Optimistic; Emphasizes 'sell-out' strategy over 'sell-in'; Confident in margin sustainability despite energy volatility; Pragmatic on short-term demand fluctuations but bullish on long-term organized sector tailwinds.
non-obvious takeaways: Company has utilized biofuels in spray dryers (Sikandrabad) for 7-8 years, insulating partially from gas shocks compared to peers; The 20% price hike is viewed as a 'one-off' realization boost that may readjust in 3-4 months, but the working capital strain on competitors creates a durable moat.

|---|---|---|---|---|

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Orient Bell Limited manufactures and sells ceramic wall and floor tiles and vitrified tiles, including glazed vitrified tiles (GVT), through strategically located manufacturing facilities and an extensive retail network across India. Internally the business is run as ceramic and vitrified-polished divisions, and it has extended into tile adhesives and bonding chemicals under the 'Master Bond' brand; the Company reports a total manufacturing capacity of 42.4 MSM per annum, over 4,000 SKUs and more than 2,000 business partners.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Vitrified capacity utilization ~80%; Ceramic lines ~90%; Adhesives in pilot/expansion phase across North & East India with new epoxy/grout launches; Anti-static tiles gaining traction but negligible revenue contribution currently.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:

- **Adhesives and bonding chemicals:** Master Bond
- **Digital platforms and tools:** InstaLook App, QuickLook tile visualisation solution, Tilekart tile commerce platform, OBL Connect channel-partner platform

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: No formal numerical guidance; Management expects margin trajectory to continue QoQ; Capex limited to maintenance (INR 10cr +/- INR 4-5cr for FY27); Volume growth dependent on gas availability and Morbi normalization.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Market share consolidation from unorganized/Morbi players shutting down; Geographic expansion of Adhesives segment; Digital lead generation converting 350+ dealers monthly; Premium mix shift via AI visualization tools.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management remains optimistic about strengthening growth momentum in the coming years with continued improvement in profitability
- Higher sales volumes are expected to result in better economies of scale, enabling absorption of fixed costs and enhancing operating leverage
- Gross margins improved to 36.4% on cost-optimisation and efficiency initiatives, which contributed like-to-like savings of 3.2% during the year
- Strong consumer shift from small-format tiles to large slabs and vitrified tiles is expected to drive higher realisation per square meter and better margins
- Continued government push for housing and infrastructure is driving steady tile consumption; projects launched in previous years now entering completion stages are expected to create sustained volume growth
- Supply disruptions and regional constraints, especially in the Morbi cluster, are enabling organised players to gain market share from smaller unorganised units
- Digital transformation in design and sales - 3D visualisation, AI deployment and digital catalogues - is improving customer engagement, while online B2B platforms help dealers order faster and reduce inventory cycles
- The 'Master Bond' adhesives and bonding-chemicals line is framed as a low-capital growth opportunity riding the established distribution system
- Headwind: Morbi overcapacity and periodic shutdowns lead to price-cutting and dumping in the domestic market, pressuring average selling prices
- Headwind: dependence on PNG/LNG - any supply disruption can halt production and there are limited alternative energy substitution options at scale
- Headwind: Middle East export exposure and rising protectionist trade measures plus USD/INR volatility pose structural risk to costs and margins

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gas prices averaged INR 45/SCM in Q4 (up ~30% YoY); Power & Fuel cost up 34% YoY driven by 20-25% production volume increase; 20% price hike (March/April) fully offset input cost inflation; Marketing spend at 3.6%, targeting ~4%.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt-free status achieved with negative net debt of INR 29cr; Strong cash conversion cycle improved to 20 days (from 26); DSO reduced by 9 days to 48 days; Focus on working capital discipline and liquidity for M&A or organic opportunities.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report discloses no new greenfield plant, brownfield line or capacity-addition project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. Installed footprint is described only as a total manufacturing capacity of 42.4 MSM per annum. Expansion in FY26 is channel-, product- and platform-led rather than capacity-led: the Company strengthened its retail-led growth strategy through Orient Bell Tile Boutiques, where the focus during FY26 was on improving the quality, size and productivity of existing showrooms along with selective expansion in key markets, and deepened its presence in the Western region while maintaining its core North and East India markets; it is actively expanding the dealer network across South India, supported by brand-building and marketing. On the product side, the Company piloted tile adhesives during the year and, after the pilot launch, adhesives are being rolled out across markets and are expected to scale up gradually - an entry into adhesives and bonding chemicals under the 'Master Bond' brand explicitly framed as building on the established distribution system while keeping capital investment low. Portfolio expansion took the form of 526 new GVT SKUs and 247 ceramic SKUs launched in FY26 rather than new lines. The Company also continued to invest in digital and AI platforms for content, channel partners and the sales force, and in national brand building. Financially, disciplined capital allocation and healthy cash generation kept the Company net debt-free, described as providing adequate financial flexibility to support future growth opportunities.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously Optimistic; Emphasizes 'sell-out' strategy over 'sell-in'; Confident in margin sustainability despite energy volatility; Pragmatic on short-term demand fluctuations but bullish on long-term organized sector tailwinds.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Premium mix and product-innovation moat: vitrified tiles contribute approximately 60% of total sales and GVT salience increased to 42%, with 526 new GVT SKUs and 247 ceramic SKUs launched in FY26
- Technology/digital differentiation: recognised as a 'tech company' in the industry, with AI-based visualisation tools that have garnered nearly a million views on InstaLook and doubled usage at activated shops, letting dealers send instant designs over WhatsApp
- Owned intellectual property: three patents, covering Scratch-Free 'Forever tiles', 'Anti-Microbial and Anti-Viral Ceramic tile' and 'Anti-static Tile'
- Retail-led distribution: Orient Bell Tile Boutiques accounted for approximately 40% of total sales, supported by 2,000+ business partners and 4,000+ SKUs
- Cost leadership: a 3.2% like-for-like year-on-year reduction in cost of production in FY26, with gross margins historically between 35% and 38% described as among the best in the industry
- Energy sourcing advantage: stronger sourcing arrangements and long-term gas contracts allowed the Company to manage the March 2026 gas-price spike better than unorganised players, leading to incremental market share gains
- Balance-sheet strength: virtually debt-free with a cash conversion cycle of 20 days as at March 31, 2026, reflecting tight control over inventory and receivables
- Brand investment: presence on television every day of the year plus digital platforms, building recall with both B2B customers and B2C consumers
- Experienced leadership team and committed workforce, guided by the 'Sarv Neta Vikreta' leadership-led execution philosophy

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Sustained high gas prices impacting demand elasticity; Labor shortages in Morbi delaying competitor recovery; Short-term demand blips due to interest rate hikes/austerity; Dealer inventory de-stocking due to price volatility.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Company has utilized biofuels in spray dryers (Sikandrabad) for 7-8 years, insulating partially from gas shocks compared to peers; The 20% price hike is viewed as a 'one-off' realization boost that may readjust in 3-4 months, but the working capital strain on competitors creates a durable moat.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |

| Gas crisis forced 500+ Morbi units to shut/reduce output; labor shortages hinder restart; working capital squeeze prevents restocking at higher prices. | Orient Bell Limited | beneficiary | High | Debt-free balance sheet allows uninterrupted production and dealer support; multi-location manufacturing reduces single-point gas allocation risk; digital 'sell-out' model bypasses distributor inventory bloating. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Digital] "Built a technology-enabled ecosystem with QuickLook, PMT, Lakshya, OBL Connect including AI-powered platforms like InstaLook and Drishti, enhancing customer experience, sales productivity and data-driven decision-making across the value chain." The deck closes with the tagline "Digitalised To Differentiate".
- [Associate entities] Two of the five manufacturing facilities are associate entities rather than owned, and the 42.4 MSM headline capacity is explicitly stated as "including AE" - group manufacturing footprint is therefore wider than the owned asset base; the income statement separately carries a "Share of Profit/(Loss) of Associates" line.
- [Outlook framing] "OBL is geared up for its next phase of growth, firing on all cylinders."
